beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Artificial Impossibility explores useful projects that cannot find anyone willing to support them.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Potential sponsors can follow reasonable rules while leaving the whole benefit unsupported.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book maps those refusals without treating every barrier as a conspiracy.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Some obstacles protect rights, so moving a boundary also requires judgment.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A purchasing assistant becomes a test when its best result is buying nothing.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its distinctive move is to compare projects through their selection environments.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That gives readers a way to question what we too quickly call unrealistic.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Consider the book’s example of an assistant that helps people buy less.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It recommends repair, reveals hidden costs, and finishes when no purchase is needed.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Those actions could serve the user while undermining advertising and affiliate revenue.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The technology’s best behavior damages its easiest way to earn money.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A better sales pitch cannot remove that conflict without changing the project.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This example shows why the book studies selection systems alongside technical feasibility.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The reader learns to ask whether an accepted business form destroys the intended value.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book’s method begins by describing the valuable outcome before choosing an organizational form.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Who benefits, including people who never become paying customers?
